preconditions.description: The number of vertices in the tree is an integer between 2 and 100 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects two distinct vertices numbered from 1 to n.
The input defines a tree with exactly n-1 edges.

preconditions.expression: all(u != v for u, v in edges)
preconditions.description: No self-loops exist in the tree.

preconditions.expression: not any((u1, v1) == (u2, v2) or (u1, v1) == (v2, u2) for (u1, v1) in edges for (u2, v2) in edges if (u1, v1) != (u2, v2))
preconditions.description: No duplicate edges exist in the tree.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= len(path_edges) <= n - 1 for path_edges in paths)
postconditions.description: Each path consists of one or more edges from the tree.

postconditions.expression: all(all(1 <= edge <= n - 1 for edge in path_edges) for path_edges in paths)
postconditions.description: Each edge in a path is numbered from 1 to n-1 as per input order.

postconditions.expression: all(len(set(edge for path_edges in paths for edge in path_edges)) == len(edge for path_edges in paths for edge in path_edges))
postconditions.description: No edge is shared between any two paths (pairwise edge-disjoint).

postconditions.expression: all(all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and (u, v) in edge_map or (v, u) in edge_map for u, v, x in path_info) for path_info in path_infos)
postconditions.description: For each path, the chosen edge (u, v) exists in the tree, and the direction is valid.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= x <= 1 for _, _, _, x in path_infos)
postconditions.description: The distance x for each point is between 0 and 1 inclusive.

postconditions.expression: all(any(vertex in path_vertices for path_vertices in path_vertices_list) for vertex in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: Every vertex from 1 to n is included in at least one selected path.
The maximum stopwatch time at vertex 1 (res1) is minimized. If multiple solutions exist, the solution with the smallest res2 is chosen, and so on lexicographically for res3, res4, ..., resn.
